{{Short description|New Zealand-British academic (1931–2024)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2018}}
{{Use British English|date=March 2018}}
'''Colwyn Trevarthen''' (2 March 1931 - 1 July 2024) was a New Zealand-British academic who was Professor of Child Psychology and Psychobiology at the [[University of Edinburgh]].

==Background==
Trevarthen was born in [[Auckland]], New Zealand on 2 March 1931.<ref name="DelgadoStrawn2014">{{cite book|author1=Sergio V. Delgado|author2=Jeffrey R. Strawn|author3=Ernest V. Pedapati|title=Contemporary Psychodynamic Psychotherapy for Children and Adolescents: Integrating Intersubjectivity and Neuroscience|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=38ioBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA69|date=2 December 2014|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-642-40520-4|page=69}}</ref> After training as a biologist in New Zealand at [[Auckland University College]] and [[Otago University]], Trevarthen researched infancy at [[Harvard University|Harvard]] in 1967. He died on 1 July 2024, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Colwyn Trevarthen (1931–2024) |url=https://perspectives.waimh.org/2024/09/13/professor-colwyn-trevarthen-1931-2024/ |website=Perspectives |access-date=10 October 2024 |date=13 September 2024}}</ref>

==Work==
Trevarthen published on brain development, infant communication and emotional health. He believed that very young babies rapidly develop proto-cultural intelligence through interacting with other people, including in teasing fun play.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web |url=http://www.psych.uw.edu.pl/lasc/Trevarthen2.pdf |title=Abstract |website=www.psych.uw.edu.pl |access-date=21 March 2014 |archive-date=22 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180722042247/http://www.psych.uw.edu.pl/lasc/Trevarthen2.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://autismandunderstanding.com/authors_04.html |title=Autism and Understanding |access-date=2014-03-21 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322013439/http://autismandunderstanding.com/authors_04.html |archive-date=2014-03-22 }}</ref> For instance he demonstrated that a newborn had an innate ability to initiate a dialogic relationship with an adult, and then build up this relationship through eye contact, smiling, and other holistic body functions rhythmically and cooperatively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jyu.fi/en/news/archive/2012/04/tapahtuma-2012-04-12-09-57-37-259587 |title=Jyväskylän yliopisto |publisher=Jyu.fi |access-date=2018-07-19}}</ref>

He studied successful interactions between infants and their primary care givers, and found that the mother's responsiveness to her baby's initiatives supported and developed intersubjectivity (shared understanding), which he regarded as the basis of all effective communication, interaction and learning.<ref name="Archived copy">{{Cite web |url=http://www.videointeractionguidance.net/background.html# |title=Background of video interaction guidance |access-date=21 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140317194831/http://www.videointeractionguidance.net/background.html# |archive-date=17 March 2014 |url-status=dead|df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="seerx">{{cite web |title=Video Interaction Guidance (V.I.G.) |url=http://www.ltscotland.org.uk/inclusiveeducation/images/VideoInteractionGuidanceVIG_tcm4-364925_tcm4-364925.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070112224841/http://www.ltscotland.org.uk/inclusiveeducation/images/VideoInteractionGuidanceVIG_tcm4-364925_tcm4-364925.pdf |archive-date=12 January 2007 |url-status=dead |publisher=LT Scotland}}</ref>

He applied [[intersubjectivity]] to the very rapid cultural development of new born infants.<ref name="autogenerated1"/> and used the term ‘primary intersubjectivity’ to refer to early developing sensory-motor processes of interaction between infants and caregivers.<ref>Trevarthen, C. B. 1979. Communication and cooperation in early infancy: A description of primary intersubjectivity. In M. Bullowa (ed.), Before Speech. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press</ref> He believes babies are looking for companionship (including the sense of fun and playfulness), engagement and relationship (rather than using the term [[attachment theory|attachment]]), and that companions can include mothers, fathers, other adults, peers and siblings; he has said ''"I think the ideal companion – and it can be a practitioner or not – is a familiar person who really treats the baby with playful human respect."''<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.educationscotland.gov.uk/video/p/video_tcm4637506.asp# |title=Professor Colwyn Trevarthen: Relationships - Video |access-date=21 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322013441/http://www.educationscotland.gov.uk/video/p/video_tcm4637506.asp# |archive-date=22 March 2014 |url-status=dead|df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In later years his work focused on the musicality of babies, including its use in communication.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iriss.org.uk/resources/why-attachment-matters-sharing-meaning-colwyn-trevarthen |title=Why attachment matters in sharing meaning - Colwyn Trevarthen |publisher=Iriss |date=2009-09-11 |access-date=2018-07-19|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o2cyg2ESltkC&q=Colwyn+Trevarthen&pg=PA281 |title=On Being Moved: From Mirror Neurons to Empathy - Google Books |date= January 2007|isbn=978-9027252043 |access-date=2018-07-19|last1=Bråten |first1=Stein }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://vimeo.com/17855175 |title=Colwyn Trevarthen - Human Nature and Early Experience on Vimeo |publisher=Vimeo.com |date=2010-12-15 |access-date=2018-07-19}}</ref>

He was a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40104|title=Gruppe 3: Filosofi og psykologi|publisher=Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters|language=Norwegian|access-date=30 March 2016|archive-date=27 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927171625/http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40104|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Video interaction guidance==
In the 1980s Harry Biemans, in the Netherlands, applied Trevarthen's research using video clips and created [[Video interaction guidance|video interaction guidance (VIG)]], which is used for instance with mothers and young babies in [[attachment-based therapy]].<ref name="Archived copy"/><ref name="seerx"/>

==Quote==
Stephen Seligman<ref>{{cite web|url=http://postdocpsychoanalytic.as.nyu.edu/object/faculty.stephen.seligman |title=Postdoctoral Program in Psychotherapy and Psychoanalysis |publisher=Postdocpsychoanalytic.as.nyu.edu |date=2018-03-19 |access-date=2018-07-19}}</ref> said Trevarthen ''"has distinguished himself for more than four decades as one of the most inventive and rigorous explorers of infant development and its implications. Among the infant research cognoscenti, he ranks... in breaking misleading assumptions of the varied disciplines to see what mothers and babies really do."''<ref>Seligman, 2009, "Anchoring intersubjective models..." Psychoanalytical Dialogues 19, p504, quoted in Video Interaction Guidance, Kennedy.</ref>
